claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni.
The baseline alloy can be processed into a single-phase FCC microstructure.
Increasing the Al/Cr ratio promotes formation of a protective dual oxide film.
The promoted dual oxide film consists predominantly of α-Al2O3 and Cr2O3.
The protective oxide film stabilizes the underlying FCC solid-solution matrix.
Stabilization of the FCC matrix suppresses phase instabilities.
Phase instabilities would degrade high-temperature strength.
Phase instabilities would degrade radiation tolerance.
Phase instabilities would degrade environmental resistance.
FCC deformation mechanisms, including deformation twinning, are responsible for cryogenic toughness.
A higher Al/Cr ratio increases the thermodynamic driving force for stable alumina formation in conjunction with Cr2O3.
The dual oxide scale minimizes further oxidation.
The oxide scale limits defect clustering.
Limiting defect clustering supports radiation tolerance.
The oxide scale preserves dislocation and twinning mechanisms in the FCC matrix.
The higher-Al/Cr alloy will have a higher fraction of α-Al2O3 and Cr2O3 after high-temperature exposure than the baseline.
The higher-Al/Cr alloy will better retain high-temperature mechanical properties than the baseline.
The higher-Al/Cr alloy will exhibit better radiation resistance than the baseline.
The higher-Al/Cr alloy will maintain or slightly enhance cryogenic toughness through sustained deformation twinning.
The hypothesis is limited to a compositional range that avoids brittle BCC phases and undesirable intermetallic precipitates.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is framed as applying to an equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy, but increasing Al relative to Cr makes the modified alloy non-equiatomic unless the phrase refers only to the baseline.

Radiation resistance is presented as a predicted and falsifiable outcome, but neither irradiation conditions nor a direct radiation-damage measurement are included in the experiment; therefore failure or improvement in radiation tolerance cannot be established by the stated design.
